REQ-DESIGN-GOALS-AND-NON-GOALS.coverage_note: Design goals are covered by cross-subsystem scenarios, but some dependent requirements still rely on modeled evidence rather than full boot/syscall/service-path enforcement.

negative_tests.name: policy mediation denies zero-authority requests without user grants
immutable base verification rejects mutable signer and measurement tampering

REQ-USERSPACE-SERVICES-BY-DEFAULT.coverage_note: Service catalog and driver/service boundaries model the split, but kernel shim exclusions are still checked partly by source markers instead of an end-to-end userspace service proof.

negative_tests.name: storage volume rejects corrupted slot payloads
service registry rejects internal interface names and unversioned API bypasses
syscall surface rejects unsupported native operations
attestation service does not count hidden requests and detects tampering
derive rejects rights and scope escalation
object store supports every native object type and rejects unsigned metadata
workspace restore rejects tampered signed snapshots
task runtime service refuses restart before a checkpoint exists

REQ-KERNEL-TYPE-AND-BOUNDARY.coverage_note: The typed native kernel boundary is implemented, but the microkernel boundary claim still depends on modeled service contracts and kernel shim marker checks.

REQ-KERNEL-REQUIREMENTS.coverage_note: Typed syscall and capability checks exist, but service restart/resource accounting isolation is not yet proven through the real freestanding syscall path for every requirement.

negative_tests.name: recovery environment audits break-glass recovery authorization
policy objects reject oversized lists and refuse authorization after tampering

REQ-BOOT-CHAIN.coverage_note: Measured boot and smoke tests exercise the boot story, but the boot chain still uses modeled artifact measurements and does not yet verify real bootloader-provided measurements end to end.

negative_tests.name: attestation service does not count hidden requests and detects tampering
recovery environment requires recovery profile and refuses missing repair targets
package service rejects invalid signatures and rollback before any update
runtime negative proofs reject modeled bypasses

REQ-COMPONENT-MODEL.coverage_note: The typed ABI validator and contract registry exist, but component interop is still modeled rather than exercised by distinct real userspace service implementations.

negative_tests.name: background dispatch throttles delayed work and denies abusive budgets

REQ-CAPABILITY-BASED-ACCESS-CONTROL.coverage_note: Capability table enforcement is implemented, but full protected-resource mediation is not yet proven across all real service paths.

negative_tests.name: policy mediation denies zero-authority requests without user grants
adversarial raw IP or domain knowledge cannot substitute for egress capability

REQ-PROCESS-ISOLATION.coverage_note: Runtime and freestanding probes cover isolation claims, but several proofs are modeled and do not yet constitute broad process-isolation enforcement across real app/service workloads.

negative_tests.name: secure secret store reports missing handles and oversized secrets

REQ-LOCAL-FIRST-REPLICATION.coverage_note: Sync state, adapters, and transport harnesses model local-first behavior, but replication is not yet proven through live multi-device service execution.

REQ-SYNC-SEMANTICS.coverage_note: CRDT/chunk/secret/database adapters are tested in-process, but they are not yet exercised as real sync service semantics over live replication paths.

negative_tests.name: workspace sharing acts as a mutable policy container
egress broker binds connection creation to attested pinned service identity
network policy connections can require remote attestation and pinned service identities
egress broker requires a usable network policy capability before connecting

REQ-PRIVATE-OVERLAY.coverage_note: Overlay sessions and relay hardening are modeled with harnesses; real encrypted overlay networking is not yet enforced end to end.

REQ-TASK-FIRST-UX.coverage_note: Task-first UX is represented by compositor/session scenarios and render strings, not by a real interactive compositor path.

REQ-WINDOWS-AND-VIEWS.coverage_note: Window/view support is scenario-rendered in the compositor model, not yet enforced by a real UI compositor.

negative_tests.name: review service rejects invalid manifests before auditing
media print service rejects remote printing and hidden jobs stay silent

REQ-UNIFIED-RESOURCE-SCHEDULER.coverage_note: Resource classes and accelerator decisions are modeled, but there is no live unified scheduler coordinating real CPU/GPU/NPU/media resources.

negative_tests.name: shared memory objects map unmap and revoke across tasks

REQ-THERMAL-AND-POWER-POLICY.coverage_note: Thermal and power policy decisions are covered by scheduler model tests, not live runtime scheduling enforcement.

REQ-USERSPACE-DRIVERS.coverage_note: Driver service authority and runtime behavior are modeled, while kernel shim boundaries still rely partly on marker checks and bootstrap inventory paths.

REQ-DRIVER-PERMISSIONS.coverage_note: Driver authority narrowing is implemented in the driver service model, but not yet proven through real driver process launch and device operations.

REQ-DRIVER-HOT-SWAP-AND-FAILURE-RECOVERY.coverage_note: Supervisor restart diagnostics are implemented in-process; real driver crash/restart recovery is not yet exercised end to end.

REQ-BASE-OS-UPDATES.coverage_note: Immutable-base and update-health flows are covered, but activation/rollback still uses modeled image state rather than a real image boot/rollback cycle.
